name: Cristiano Ronaldo
ratingRationale: All-time UCL record goalscorer (140 goals) and 5-time winner with unmatched knockout-stage clutch scoring across three decades.
keyHighlight: Record 17 goals in the 2013-14 campaign and hat-tricks against Bayern, Atlético, and Wolfsburg.

name: Lionel Messi
ratingRationale: 4-time Champions League champion, scoring 129 goals in 163 games with supreme playmaking and solo final goals in 2009 and 2011.
keyHighlight: Masterclass display and wonder goal in the 2011 final at Wembley; iconic solo goal vs Real Madrid in 2011 semi-final.

name: Paolo Maldini
ratingRationale: Played in 8 European Cup/UCL finals, winning 5 titles across three decades (1989, 1990, 1994, 2003, 2007) as defensive royalty.
keyHighlight: Captain of Milan's 2003 and 2007 triumphs and scored after 52 seconds in the 2005 final.

name: Zinedine Zidane
ratingRationale: Scored arguably the greatest goal in tournament history to seal the 2002 title for Real Madrid.
keyHighlight: Iconic left-foot volley from Roberto Carlos' cross in the 2002 Hampden Park final vs Bayer Leverkusen.

name: Sergio Ramos
ratingRationale: 4-time winner whose 92:48 stoppage-time header in Lisbon 2014 delivered La Décima, alongside immense knockout goalscoring.
keyHighlight: 93rd minute equalizer in the 2014 Final vs Atlético Madrid and goal in the 2016 Final.

name: Karim Benzema
ratingRationale: 5-time champion and 4th all-time top scorer (90 goals), with a legendary 15-goal campaign in 2021-22 delivering unforgettable comebacks.
keyHighlight: Back-to-back hat-tricks against PSG and Chelsea in the 2021-22 knockouts followed by deciding goals vs Man City.

name: Luka Modrić
ratingRationale: Joint-record 6-time UCL winner whose outside-of-the-boot passing and press resistance anchored Real Madrid's historic modern era.
keyHighlight: Trivela assist for Rodrygo vs Chelsea in 2022 quarter-final and corner assist for Ramos' 93rd minute goal in 2014.

name: Xavi Hernández
ratingRationale: The heartbeat of Barcelona's golden era, controlling tempos with 151 UCL appearances and 4 Champions League medals.
keyHighlight: Masterclass assists in the 2009 and 2011 finals against Manchester United.

name: Andrés Iniesta
ratingRationale: Man of the Match in the 2015 final, 4-time champion who glided through defenses in the biggest European nights.
keyHighlight: Stoppage-time outside-the-box missile at Stamford Bridge in 2009 to send Barcelona to Rome.

name: Manuel Neuer
ratingRationale: Revolutionized the goalkeeper position with sweeper-keeper mastery; two-time Treble winner with 58 clean sheets.
keyHighlight: Unbeatable performances in Lisbon 2020 final vs PSG and Wembley 2013 vs Dortmund.

name: Iker Casillas
ratingRationale: 3-time winner who became the youngest goalkeeper to win a final in 2000 and accumulated 59 clean sheets across 177 games.
keyHighlight: Crucial late saves as an emergency substitute in the 2002 Hampden Park final against Leverkusen.

name: Philipp Lahm
ratingRationale: Flawless tactical intelligence, captained Bayern Munich to the 2013 Champions League title playing both fullback flanks and midfield.
keyHighlight: Lifting the 2013 trophy at Wembley after playing every minute of Bayern's historic treble knockout run.

name: Robert Lewandowski
ratingRationale: 94 UCL goals (3rd all-time); scored 15 goals in 10 matches during Bayern's flawless 2019-20 Champions League triumph.
keyHighlight: 4 goals against Real Madrid in the 2013 semi-final for Dortmund; top scorer of the 2020 winning campaign.

name: Clarence Seedorf
ratingRationale: The only player in football history to win the UEFA Champions League with three different clubs (Ajax 1995, Real Madrid 1998, Milan 2003 & 2007).
keyHighlight: Midfield dominance across 125 games and 4 European titles.

name: Toni Kroos
ratingRationale: Joint-record 6-time winner with unmatched pass completion metrics under highest European pressure.
keyHighlight: Final club game winning the 2024 Wembley final with assist for Carvajal's breakthrough header.

name: Raúl González
ratingRationale: 3-time winner who scored in two different finals (2000 & 2002) and held the all-time scoring record for over a decade with 71 goals.
keyHighlight: Solo breakaway goal in the 2000 final vs Valencia and silencing the Camp Nou.

name: Thierry Henry
ratingRationale: 50 goals in 112 matches, finalist with Arsenal in 2006 and lifted the trophy with Barcelona's 2009 treble side.
keyHighlight: Solo masterpiece goal vs Real Madrid at the Santiago Bernabéu in 2006.

name: Steven Gerrard
ratingRationale: Leader of the 'Miracle of Istanbul' in 2005, initiating Liverpool's comeback from 0-3 down against AC Milan.
keyHighlight: Inspirational header in 2005 Istanbul final and dramatic late screamer vs Olympiacos in group stage.

name: Dani Alves
ratingRationale: 3-time UCL winner with Barcelona, redefined the attacking right-back role with relentless dynamism and linkup play.
keyHighlight: Dominant showings in Barcelona's 2011 and 2015 tournament triumphs and Juventus 2017 run.

name: Roberto Carlos
ratingRationale: 3-time champion with Real Madrid (1998, 2000, 2002) and 120 UCL caps, famed for ferocious long-range strikes and crosses.
keyHighlight: High looping cross for Zidane's timeless volley in the 2002 final in Glasgow.

name: Marcelo
ratingRationale: 5-time winner who combined dazzling dribbling and pinpoint crossing on the left flank for Real Madrid's dynasty.
keyHighlight: Extra-time goal in the 2014 final and crucial assists in 2017 and 2018 finals.

name: Carles Puyol
ratingRationale: 3-time winning captain (2006, 2009, 2011) known for heroic goal-line stops and passionate defensive leadership.
keyHighlight: Handed captain's armband to Eric Abidal to lift the 2011 trophy at Wembley following his cancer recovery.

name: Alessandro Nesta
ratingRationale: The gold standard of slide-tackling and defensive elegance, winning 2 titles in Milan's legendary backline.
keyHighlight: Penalty shootout conversion in the 2003 final at Old Trafford and commanding display in 2007 Athens final.

name: Arjen Robben
ratingRationale: 89th minute Wembley winner in 2013 capped a decade of lethal cutting inside and 31 UCL goals in 110 games.
keyHighlight: Scored the dramatic 89th-minute winner vs Dortmund in the 2013 all-German final at Wembley.

name: Thomas Müller
ratingRationale: 2-time Treble champion with 54 goals across 150+ appearances, universally acclaimed as the ultimate Raumdeuter.
keyHighlight: Goal in 2012 final and 8 goals in Bayern's 2013 and 2020 treble-winning campaigns.

name: Gerard Piqué
ratingRationale: 4-time UCL winner (Man United 2008, Barcelona 2009, 2011, 2015) and 16 goals in 128 games as an elite ball-playing center-back.
keyHighlight: Immaculate defensive performance in the 2009 Rome final and 2011 Wembley final.

name: Andrea Pirlo
ratingRationale: Architect of deep-lying playmaking, winning 2 Champions League titles with Milan (2003, 2007) and reaching the 2015 final with Juventus.
keyHighlight: Free-kick deflection assist for Inzaghi in the 2007 Athens final revenge against Liverpool.

name: Kaká
ratingRationale: Top scorer of the 2006-07 UCL with 10 goals, leading Milan to the title with unstoppable acceleration and vision.
keyHighlight: Sublime solo goals against Manchester United in both legs of the 2007 semi-final at Old Trafford and San Siro.

name: Kevin De Bruyne
ratingRationale: Playmaking genius of Manchester City's 2023 treble triumph, delivering 25+ UCL assists and crucial knockout goals.
keyHighlight: Stunning low rocket from 25 yards at the Bernabéu in the 2023 semi-final first leg.

name: Casemiro
ratingRationale: The anchor of Real Madrid's 5 UCL crowns (2014, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2022), providing ruthless defensive solidity.
keyHighlight: Long-range deflected thunderbolt to make it 2-1 in the 2017 Cardiff final against Juventus.

name: Gianluigi Buffon
ratingRationale: 3-time finalist with 124 appearances and 53 clean sheets, renowned for supreme positioning across two decades.
keyHighlight: Instinctive one-handed save to deny Inzaghi's point-blank header in the 2003 Old Trafford final.

name: Samuel Eto'o
ratingRationale: Won back-to-back trebles with two different clubs (Barcelona 2009, Inter 2010), scoring in two finals (2006 & 2009).
keyHighlight: Equalizer against Arsenal in Paris 2006 and opening goal against Man United in Rome 2009.

name: Andriy Shevchenko
ratingRationale: 48 goals in 100 UCL matches; top scorer in 1999 and 2006, won the 2003 title with the decisive shootout penalty.
keyHighlight: Winning penalty in the 2003 Manchester final shootout vs Juventus and hat-trick at the Camp Nou for Dynamo Kyiv in 1997.

name: Edwin van der Sar
ratingRationale: Won UCL titles 13 years apart (Ajax 1995, Man United 2008) and recorded 51 clean sheets in 130 games.
keyHighlight: Saved Nicolas Anelka's penalty in the rain in Moscow 2008 to win the shootout.

name: Petr Čech
ratingRationale: 49 clean sheets; saved Robben's extra-time penalty and two shootout kicks in the 2012 'Finale Dahoam' vs Bayern.
keyHighlight: Hero of Munich 2012, guessing the right way on all six Bayern penalties (one in ET, five in shootout).

name: Oliver Kahn
ratingRationale: 'Der Titan' saved 3 penalties in the 2001 final shootout in Milan, earning Man of the Match and the Fair Play Award.
keyHighlight: Saving Mauricio Pellegrino's penalty to seal the 2001 title at San Siro.

name: Virgil van Dijk
ratingRationale: UEFA Men's Player of the Year in 2019, reached 3 finals and anchored Liverpool's victory in Madrid 2019 with peerless aerial dominance.
keyHighlight: Clean sheet and Man of the Match performance in the 2019 final against Tottenham.

name: Franck Ribéry
ratingRationale: UEFA Best Player in Europe 2013; dynamic winger whose backheel set up Robben's 89th-minute Wembley final winner.
keyHighlight: Key assist in 2013 final and tearing Barcelona apart 7-0 on aggregate in 2013 semi-final.

name: Bastian Schweinsteiger
ratingRationale: Played in 3 finals (2010, 2012, 2013), overcoming Munich heartbreak to boss the midfield in Bayern's 2013 Wembley triumph.
keyHighlight: Decisive shootout penalty at the Bernabéu in 2012 and dominant display in 2013 final.

name: Frank Lampard
ratingRationale: Captained Chelsea to 2012 glory in Munich; 23 UCL goals from midfield and scored in the 2008 Moscow final.
keyHighlight: Lofted through-ball assist for Ramires at Camp Nou in 2012 and converted shootout penalty in Munich.

name: Didier Drogba
ratingRationale: 44 goals in 92 games; 88th-minute header and deciding penalty in Munich 2012 made him Chelsea's ultimate big-game hero.
keyHighlight: Bullet header in the 88th minute of the 2012 final and calmly rolling in the trophy-winning penalty.

name: Paul Scholes
ratingRationale: 2-time winner (1999, 2008) with 124 appearances and 24 goals, lauded by Zidane and Xavi as the complete English midfielder.
keyHighlight: Unstoppable 25-yard dipping screamer against Barcelona in the 2008 semi-final at Old Trafford.

name: Sergio Busquets
ratingRationale: 3-time champion (2009, 2011, 2015) and 129 appearances, mastering positional anticipation and one-touch distribution.
keyHighlight: Flawless pivot display in the 2011 final vs Manchester United and assist for Messi's solo goal at the Bernabéu.

name: Gareth Bale
ratingRationale: 5-time winner who scored winning goals in two finals (2014 & 2018), including an iconic overhead bicycle kick.
keyHighlight: Spectacular overhead kick vs Liverpool in Kyiv 2018 and extra-time header vs Atlético in Lisbon 2014.

name: Ronaldinho
ratingRationale: Ballon d'Or winner who led Barcelona to their 2006 Paris triumph, bringing uncontainable flair and match-winning genius.
keyHighlight: Standing-toe-poke wonder goal against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in 2005.

name: Ruud van Nistelrooy
ratingRationale: Three-time UCL top scorer (2002, 2003, 2005), scoring an astounding 56 goals in just 73 appearances.
keyHighlight: Scoring 12 goals in only 9 appearances during the 2002-03 campaign for Manchester United.

name: Alessandro Del Piero
ratingRationale: 1996 champion and 4-time finalist with 42 goals in 89 matches; scored 10 goals in the 1997-98 campaign.
keyHighlight: Standing ovation at the Santiago Bernabéu in 2008 after a sublime brace for Juventus.

name: Ryan Giggs
ratingRationale: 2-time champion (1999, 2008) who scored in 16 different UCL campaigns across 145 appearances.
keyHighlight: Scored the decisive penalty in sudden death against Chelsea in Moscow 2008.

name: Javier Zanetti
ratingRationale: Captained Inter to their historic 2010 Treble in his 700th club game; 97 UCL appearances of untiring resilience.
keyHighlight: Lifting the 2010 Champions League trophy at the Bernabéu after shackling Robben and Messi.

name: Erling Haaland
ratingRationale: Fastest player in tournament history to 40 goals; top scorer with 12 goals during Man City's 2022-23 Champions League winning run.
keyHighlight: 5 goals in a single knockout match against RB Leipzig in 2023.

name: Kylian Mbappé
ratingRationale: 48 goals in 73 games by age 25; finalist in 2020 and multiple hat-tricks at the Camp Nou and Allianz Arena.
keyHighlight: Stunning hat-trick at the Camp Nou against Barcelona in the 2021 round of 16.

name: Neymar Jr
ratingRationale: Joint top scorer (10 goals) in Barcelona's 2015 winning run, sealing the final in Berlin; 43 goals and 36 assists in 81 games.
keyHighlight: Orchestrated the 6-1 'Remontada' against PSG in 2017 with two goals and the 95th minute assist.

name: Luis Suárez
ratingRationale: Scored the decisive 2-1 goal in the 2015 Berlin final; spearhead of the legendary MSN attacking trident.
keyHighlight: Double nutmeg masterclass against PSG at the Parc des Princes in 2015 and goal in the final.

name: Thibaut Courtois
ratingRationale: Record 9 saves in a Champions League final (Paris 2022 vs Liverpool), winning Man of the Match and his first European crown.
keyHighlight: Man of the Match exhibition in the 2022 final in Paris against Liverpool.

name: Rio Ferdinand
ratingRationale: Captained Manchester United in the 2008 final win in Moscow; part of the tournament's tightest defensive partnerships.
keyHighlight: Near impenetrable campaign conceding only 6 goals in 13 matches in 2007-08.

name: John Terry
ratingRationale: UEFA Club Defender of the Year three times (2005, 2008, 2009); 109 appearances and 10 goals as Chelsea's captain.
keyHighlight: Crucial 76th-minute winning header against Barcelona in the 2005 round of 16 classic.

name: David Alaba
ratingRationale: 4-time UCL winner (Bayern 2013, 2020; Real Madrid 2022, 2024), starting finals at left-back and center-back.
keyHighlight: Chair-celebration icon in 2022 comeback and defensive rock in Bayern's 2020 treble.

name: Raphaël Varane
ratingRationale: 4-time winner with Real Madrid (2014, 2016, 2017, 2018), started three finals alongside Ramos with rapid recovery pace.
keyHighlight: Started at age 21 in the 2014 Lisbon final extra-time triumph.

name: Vinícius Júnior
ratingRationale: 2-time UCL champion who scored the winning goal in the 2022 final and the clincher in the 2024 final at Wembley.
keyHighlight: 59th minute winner at Stade de France in 2022 and 83rd minute goal in 2024 final.

name: Mohamed Salah
ratingRationale: 44 goals in 80 appearances; opened scoring in the 2019 Madrid final to capture Liverpool's sixth European title.
keyHighlight: 2nd-minute penalty conversion in the 2019 final in Madrid.

name: Rodri
ratingRationale: Ballon d'Or winner and Player of the Season 2022-23; scored the only goal in Istanbul 2023 to seal Manchester City's Treble.
keyHighlight: 68th-minute controlled strike into the corner in the 2023 final against Inter Milan.

name: Cafu
ratingRationale: The tireless Brazilian fullback who started the 2005 and 2007 finals for Milan, claiming the title in Athens 2007.
keyHighlight: Lifting the 2007 trophy in Athens after a vintage defensive display.

name: Deco
ratingRationale: Named UEFA Club Footballer of the Year 2004 with Porto, then won it again in 2006 with Barcelona.
keyHighlight: Man of the Match goal and display in the 2004 final in Gelsenkirchen against Monaco.

name: Claude Makélélé
ratingRationale: Defined the defensive screening position in modern football; 2002 champion with Real Madrid.
keyHighlight: Shielded Real Madrid's Galácticos backline on the way to the 2002 Glasgow triumph.

name: Joshua Kimmich
ratingRationale: UCL Defender of the Year 2020; provided the chipped cross assist for Coman's 2020 final winner in Lisbon.
keyHighlight: Chipped assist in the 2020 final and 2024 quarter-final winning header against Arsenal.

name: Fernando Morientes
ratingRationale: 3-time winner with Real Madrid (1998, 2000, 2002), top scorer in 2003-04 with Monaco (9 goals).
keyHighlight: Opening goal in the 2000 Paris final vs Valencia and knocking out Madrid while on loan at Monaco in 2004.

name: Filippo Inzaghi
ratingRationale: 46 goals in 81 UCL matches; scored both goals in Milan's 2-1 revenge victory over Liverpool in the 2007 final.
keyHighlight: Man of the Match brace in Athens 2007 final.

name: Wayne Rooney
ratingRationale: 30 UCL goals and 3 finals; hat-trick on competition debut against Fenerbahçe and scored in 2011 final at Wembley.
keyHighlight: Debut hat-trick at age 18 in 2004 and winning the 2008 title in Moscow.

name: Rúben Dias
ratingRationale: Defensive anchor for Manchester City's 2023 treble triumph, winning UCL Defender of the Season.
keyHighlight: Block after block in the 2021 semi-final against PSG and clean sheet in 2023 final.

name: Trent Alexander-Arnold
ratingRationale: Youngest player to start two consecutive UCL finals; registered iconic assists across 3 finals appearances.
keyHighlight: 'Corner taken quickly... Origi!' vs Barcelona in the historic 2019 Anfield comeback.

name: Bernardo Silva
ratingRationale: Tireless creative engine for Manchester City's 2023 European crown; scored twice in the 4-0 demolition of Real Madrid.
keyHighlight: First-half brace against Real Madrid in the 2023 Etihad semi-final second leg.

name: Keylor Navas
ratingRationale: Starting goalkeeper for Real Madrid's historic 3-peat (2016, 2017, 2018), producing crucial knockout stage saves.
keyHighlight: Masterful 8-save showing against Bayern Munich in the 2018 semi-final second leg.

name: Alisson Becker
ratingRationale: UCL Goalkeeper of the Season 2018-19, keeping a clean sheet in the final and pulling off 8 saves against Tottenham.
keyHighlight: Stoppage time point-blank save against Milik (Napoli) to ensure qualification, and clean sheet in 2019 final.

name: Peter Schmeichel
ratingRationale: Captained Manchester United in the famous 1999 Treble final in Barcelona on his final club appearance.
keyHighlight: Star-jump cartwheel celebration after injury-time comeback goals in Barcelona 1999.

name: Giorgio Chiellini
ratingRationale: Gladiator of the 'BBC' backline that carried Juventus to the 2015 and 2017 finals, totaling 74 UCL matches.
keyHighlight: Shutting out Barcelona's MSN over 180 minutes in the 2017 quarter-finals, scoring in the first leg.

name: Franz Beckenbauer
ratingRationale: 'Der Kaiser' captained Bayern Munich to three consecutive European Cup titles (1974, 1975, 1976), pioneering the attacking libero role.
keyHighlight: 3-time consecutive European Cup winning captain and Ballon d'Or winner.

name: Gerd Müller
ratingRationale: 'Der Bomber' scored 34 goals in just 35 European Cup games (0.97 goals/game), netting in the 1974 and 1975 finals for Bayern.
keyHighlight: Brace in the 1974 replay final against Atlético Madrid and sealing the 1975 final vs Leeds.

name: Johan Cruyff
ratingRationale: The pioneer of Total Football who guided Ajax to a European Cup hat-trick (1971, 1972, 1973), scoring both goals in the 1972 final.
keyHighlight: Both goals in the 2-0 victory over Inter Milan in the 1972 final in Rotterdam.

name: Franco Baresi
ratingRationale: 3-time European champion (1989, 1990, 1994), who marshaled Milan's unbeatable backline and lifted the 1989 and 1990 trophies.
keyHighlight: Orchestrated the 4-0 thrashing of Steaua in 1989 and set defensive blueprints for modern football.

name: Marco van Basten
ratingRationale: 2-time European Cup winner with Milan; scored twice in the 1989 final and scored 4 goals in a single 1992 UCL match vs Gothenburg.
keyHighlight: Two goals in the 1989 final 4-0 win against Steaua Bucharest in Barcelona.

name: Lothar Matthäus
ratingRationale: Ballon d'Or winner and World Player of the Year, reached two European finals (1987, 1999) with commanding box-to-box dominance.
keyHighlight: Towering performances across 15 European campaigns for Bayern Munich.
